requirement:
The harness MUST expose an `outline` tool with this interface:

```text
outline({ file: String }) -> Array<OutlineEntry>

OutlineEntry {
    item: String,
    kind: String,
    name: String?,
    children: Array<OutlineEntry>,
}
```

The tool MUST return the outline of a permitted file in a supported language
under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines`, with each node's selector under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`, its kind, and its name when it
is named, nested by outline ancestry and in source order. Results MUST contain
no source text or line numbers and MUST NOT become evidence inputs; the model reads
the nodes it relies on with the `habeas` tool. For a file using the plain-text
profile, the outline lists its `line` nodes. Explicitly requesting an excluded
file MUST be handled as a denial under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
rationale:
I found no gap in the `outline` tool's code, reachability or tests. This is based on the mandatory inputs only; I did not open `Listing::array`, `pages.deliver` or `AssessmentSources::prepare`, and I read `fn[with_redaction_note]` only up to the point where its output was cut off.

**Interface**
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[definitions]` advertises `outline` with a required string `file`, `additionalProperties: false`, and a description covering selector, kind, name, no line numbers, no source text and no evidence inputs.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[dispatch_paged]` routes `"outline"` to `fn[outline]`.
- `fn[outline]` checks the argument keys and the `file` string, so malformed arguments return an error. It then calls `AssessmentSources::parse_file` and returns `Listing::array(outline_entries(...))`.
- `fn[outline_entries]` emits `{item, kind, name, children}` for each node. It uses the node's selector, its kind, and `display_name()` from `src/outline/mod.rs`, which gives null for anonymous nodes. Children are recursed in source order, which gives nesting by ancestry.
- The root node (index 0) is not listed; only its children appear. I read that as consistent with the text, and the test expects it.

**Outline content**
- `src/inputs.rs#impl[OutlineCache]/fn[parse]` reads and parses the file with the language profile chosen by `outline::profile_for_path`.
- Other text files get the plain-text profile, whose `line` nodes have `line@…` selectors. Parse failures become explanatory tool errors.
- Selector syntax and profile contents belong to the cited outline requirements, which I did not reassess.

**No source text, line numbers or evidence inputs**
- The entries carry only `item`, `kind`, `name` and `children`. The `ToolDelivery` that `pages.deliver` returns is not shown, but the test asserts `outline.inputs.is_empty()`.
- `with_redaction_note` only changes object results, and the outline result is an array.

**Denial of excluded files**
- `parse_file` calls `self.access.file(...)?` before parsing, so a disallowed file returns a `PermissionDenied` error.
- `recoverable_outside_request` turns an outside-project denial into an ordinary read failure.
- The denial's content (path and reason, no evidence added, assessment continues) is governed by the cited `requirements.authoring.read_denial`, which I did not reassess.

**Tests**
- `mod[tests]/fn[outline_lists_nested_nodes_without_text_or_inputs]` asserts:
  - the exact nested Rust result in source order;
  - no doc text and no inputs;
  - plain-text `line@` nodes with a null name and no line fields;
  - errors for a missing file and for missing arguments;
  - `PermissionDenied` for a disallowed file.
- `mod[tests]/fn[outline_tool_is_advertised_with_a_required_file_argument]` asserts the schema and the description phrases.
- `mod[tests]/fn[unpermitted_requests_outside_the_project_are_recoverable_tool_errors]` covers an outline request for a path outside the project, and the in-project denial still aborting.
- All three tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.

text: :::{req} outline_tool
The harness MUST expose an `outline` tool with this interface:
```text
outline({ file: String }) -> Array<OutlineEntry>
OutlineEntry {
item: String,
kind: String,
name: String?,
children: Array<OutlineEntry>,
The tool MUST return the outline of a permitted file in a supported language
under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines`, with each node's selector under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`, its kind, and its name when it
is named, nested by outline ancestry and in source order. Results MUST contain
no source text or line numbers and MUST NOT become evidence inputs; the model reads
the nodes it relies on with the `habeas` tool. For a file using the plain-text
profile, the outline lists its `line` nodes. Explicitly requesting an excluded
file MUST be handled as a denial under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} read_denial
When source-access policy denies a path that a model tool call names
explicitly, the harness MUST return a tool error naming the path and the reason
it cannot be read, add no evidence input, and continue the assessment.
Discovery and search MUST leave denied candidates out of their entries,
reporting untracked ones under {cite}`requirements.authoring.not_listed`. Malformed tool
arguments and ordinary read failures MUST also return explanatory tool errors.
